long_biography.plain_text:
Industrial entrepreneur Jim Bernhard brought factory methods to a trade often performed by welders on construction sites. At Shaw, he adopted fabrication technology and inventory systems developed by others, then acquired a Dutch manufacturer whose pipe-bending machines reduced welding work. The combination helped the business supply complex projects while tracking thousands of separate pipe sections.

At Pin Oak Stud, which he owned with his wife, Dana, Bernhard used sensors to monitor racehorses' movement during training. He regarded the readings as additional information for trainers, rather than a replacement for their judgement. The couple also committed to preserving the wooded areas between the Kentucky farm's paddocks.
